chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man from your mawalis conveys greetings to you and has intended to marry a woman who is compatible with him and some of her affairs have pleased him, and she had a husband who divorced her three times not according to the Sunnah, and he was reluctant to proceed with marrying her until he seeks your advice, so that you would command him.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the private part (of the body), and the matter of the private part is severe, and from it comes the child, and we are cautious, so let him not marry her.'

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private part (referring to the reproductive organ/marital act)
key_terms.غَيْرِ السُّنَّةِ: Not according to the Prophetic tradition (Sunnah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman divorced three times in a non-Sunni manner?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against this marriage to preserve the sanctity of lineage, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ihtiyat* (caution) in marital unions where the previous divorce lacked proper procedural validity. This ruling highlights the distinction between the mere legal permissibility of marrying a *mutallaqah* and the recommended prudence in avoiding potential defects in offspring or lineage clarity.
